# SaaS Agreement - section-by-section drafting guide

Template: the confirmed SaaS Agreement template (location in Engagement inputs, SKILL.md). The **master agreement** - one per client legal entity, executed once; every Marketplace/BoW app then attaches via its own Provisioning SOW (which prevails on conflict for its services). Context: this is for Marketplace/BoW **product subscriptions** - the client subscribes to a firm-built app - distinct from a services SOW.

**The single most important fact, proven by executed copies to date:** the body is standard firm legal paper and is signed essentially verbatim. Executed agreements (filenames and made-dates in Engagement inputs, SKILL.md) differ from the template ONLY in: made-date, client party block, and signature block (plus, where the client requires it, a legal-review stamp). **Zero body clauses changed.** So drafting this document = filling four blanks. Anything beyond that is a negotiated legal change - flag it as `[DEVIATION FROM TEMPLATE: ...]` and route to firm legal; do not draft substitute language.

## Fill-ins (the entire drafting job)

1. **Made date** in the opening paragraph (template still reads ", 2022" - replace the whole blank+year).
2. **Client legal name** - the exact registered legal entity (the full name, not an abbreviation or a health-system/other affiliate). Which entity signs determines which entity's apps can attach SOWs - cross-check section Application Usage limits in the SOWs.
3. **Client office address**.
4. **Signature block** - see below.

Everything else: read, verify intact, leave alone.

## Body structure (verify-intact map - 8 articles)

1. **Services** - 1.1 Statements of Work (SOW incorporates this agreement; SOW prevails on conflict); 1.2 SaaS Service (+ Documentation: user guides/training materials made generally available - wd-kt's deliverables have contractual weight here); 1.3 Professional Services (if described in a SOW, commercially-reasonable efforts); 1.4 Other Services (subscription/other pricing models; collectively "Services"); 1.5 Maintenance & Technical Support (the firm may install updates; client designates primary + escalation contact); 1.6 Suspension of Access (nonpayment 10 days, breach, network integrity, legal violation; reactivation fees).
2. **Rights** - 2.1 Right to Use (non-exclusive, non-transferable, internal business purposes, term-limited, no third-party access; FAR/DFAR commercial-item language); 2.2 Use Restrictions (no competitive use, resale, service bureau, derivative works, reverse engineering, export violations; injunctive relief); 2.3 Proprietary Rights (Services/Documentation/derivatives remain the firm's - the IP core: never touch).
3. **Data** - 3.1 Client Content (limited license to the firm to perform); 3.2 PHI (45 C.F.R. section 164.501/section 160.103; **protected per a written business associate agreement** - if the app touches PHI, confirm a BAA exists or placeholder the dependency; the BAA is a separate document this skill does not draft); 3.3 PII (use only per Agreement and client direction); 3.4 Service Provider Data (the firm may collect/aggregate de-identified usage data); 3.5 Confidential Information (mutual); 3.6 Offshore Support (data may be processed offshore - client must notify the firm of restrictions; flag to the client-facing team when the client has data-residency policies); 3.7 Rights Notices.
4. **Fees, Payment, and Taxes** - 4.1 fees per SOW, net 30 from invoice, 1.5%/month late charge; 4.2 expenses reimbursable, fees non-refundable; 4.3 long-term on-site tax gross-up; 4.4 taxes (client pays sales/use/VAT etc.; tax-exemption certificate - if the client is tax-exempt, expect the certificate); 4.5 foreign withholding.
5. **Disclaimer of Warranties** - Services AS IS, all warranties disclaimed. All-caps risk clause: never touch.
6. **Limited Liability** - cap = the firm's fees for the **last 12 months under the applicable SOW** from which the cause of action arose; no punitive/consequential/indirect damages. All-caps risk clause: never touch.
7. **Term and Termination** - 7.1 term per SOW; auto-renewal unless written notice >= **sixty (60) days** before term end (SOWs may override - the current program's SOWs say 30; SOW prevails, don't reconcile silently); services non-cancelable mid-term except for cause; 7.2 Termination for Cause (material breach, 30-day cure); 7.3 Effects of Termination (access ends, amounts due; survival: 2.3, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7.3, 8).
8. **General** - 8.1 Entire Agreement; 8.2 Reference (the firm may use client name/logo in marketing - the clause clients most often ask to strike; if asked, flag as deviation for legal, don't just delete); 8.3 Governing Law (the firm's home state) + arbitration; 8.4 Force Majeure; 8.5 Assignment (the firm may assign to successor); 8.6 Severability; 8.7 Notices; 8.8 Waiver; 8.9 No Relationship; 8.10 Non-Solicitation (1 year post-term).

## Signature block

Template: two-column, with the firm's signatory pre-filled (the template's pre-filled Managing Director name). Use the client's executed pattern (specific firm signer and client entity blocks in Engagement inputs, SKILL.md): the firm side signed by the firm's authorized signatory; client side = the client legal-entity block(s), plus any required legal-department review/stamp line where the client spans multiple entities. For new paper on a client with executed precedent use that pattern; otherwise placeholder the firm signer (`[FIRM SIGNER - needs: current authorized signatory from the firm's contracts team]`) rather than copying a prior name.

## Cross-checks before handoff

- Made-date here is what every future SOW must cite as "SaaS Agreement dated ___" - record it; SOW/agreement date mismatches have occurred (a draft SOW citing a date matching neither executed master - the executed made-dates are in Engagement inputs, SKILL.md).
- A client may have more than one executed master (see Engagement inputs) - before drafting any new SOW, confirm with the MD which one it attaches under.
- PHI-touching app -> BAA dependency noted; client with offshore-data restrictions -> 3.6 flag.
- Client requires breach-notification terms -> confirm the BAA or a data-protection addendum covers it; the body map above has **no breach-notification clause** - if the master is silent and no addendum exists, flag as `[DEVIATION FROM TEMPLATE: breach notification]` for legal rather than drafting one.
- Append the standard Open Placeholders & Deviations list and DRAFT stamp (SKILL.md markup rules).
